lectures.title: Course introduction and overview
lectures.summary: The seminar opens with a course introduction and overview. Discussion covers the nature of imagination, the eccentric genius, divine inspiration, and bisociation, together with the roles of dreaming and the unconscious in creativity.

lectures.title: Consummation and love; intuition versus intelligence; creativity types
lectures.summary: After a review of Session 1, the discussion takes up consummation and love and intuition versus intelligence, and considers the types of creativity: logical, empirical, moral, practical, and others.

lectures.title: Creativity, religion, and the nature of the universe
lectures.summary: The session discusses creativity, religion, and the nature of the universe, drawing on theories of creativity and imagination from Bergson, Plato, Nietzsche, Minsky, Boden, Freud, and Proust.

lectures.title: Students present research paper topics
lectures.summary: Students present their research paper topics, which include the brain as a bodily instrument, capitalism and economics in relation to creativity, creativity in a cappella singing, and human versus computer creativity.
